# Issue #47: flag parsing treats "off " as true

A setting written as `off ` with a trailing space ends up enabled. This showed up
when reading feature switches from the environment. Please fix the flag parsing.


Repository files:
flags/__init__.py
flags/parse.py
tests/test_parse.py

1| """Parsing of on/off switches from configuration text."""
   2| 
   3| _FALSE_WORDS = frozenset({"0", "false", "no", "off"})
   4| 
   5| 
   6| def parse_flag(text):
   7|     """Interpret one switch word as a bool.
   8| 
   9|     Matching is case-insensitive and ignores whitespace around the word.
  10|     "0", "false", "no" and "off" are False; any other non-empty word is True.
  11|     Raises ValueError if the text is empty or only whitespace.
  12|     """
  13|     word = text.lower()
  14|     if not word:
  15|         raise ValueError("empty flag")
  16|     return word not in _FALSE_WORDS
  17| 
  18| 
  19| def parse_flags(text):
  20|     """Parse a comma-separated list of switch words into a list of bools.
  21| 
  22|     Each item is interpreted with `parse_flag`. Items that are empty or only
  23|     whitespace are skipped, so "" gives [] and "on,,off" gives [True, False].
  24|     """
  25|     return [parse_flag(part) for part in text.split(",") if part.strip()]

1| import unittest
   2| from flags import parse_flag, parse_flags
   3| 
   4| 
   5| class TestFlags(unittest.TestCase):
   6|     def test_words(self):
   7|         self.assertTrue(parse_flag("on"))
   8|         self.assertTrue(parse_flag("YES"))
   9|         self.assertFalse(parse_flag("off"))
  10|         self.assertFalse(parse_flag("False"))
  11| 
  12|     def test_list(self):
  13|         self.assertEqual(parse_flags("on,off,yes"), [True, False, True])
  14| 
  15|     def test_list_with_spaces(self):
  16|         self.assertEqual(parse_flags("on, off ,yes"), [True, False, True])
  17| 
  18| 
  19| if __name__ == "__main__":
  20|     unittest.main()

The bug is clear: `parse_flag` lowercases but never strips whitespace, so `"off "` doesn't match `"off"` and falls through to `True` — contradicting its own docstring ("ignores whitespace around the word"). The empty check also fails to catch whitespace-only input.

arguments.old:
word = text.lower()
    if not word:
        raise ValueError("empty flag")
    return word not in _FALSE_WORDS
arguments.new:
word = text.strip().lower()
    if not word:
        raise ValueError("empty flag")
    return word not in _FALSE_WORDS

arguments.summary: Fixed issue #47 in flags/parse.py: `parse_flag` lowercased the input but never stripped whitespace, so `"off "` (trailing space) didn't match the false-word set and was treated as True. Changed `text.lower()` to `text.strip().lower()`, which makes the function honor its documented behavior ("ignores whitespace around the word") and also makes whitespace-only input correctly raise ValueError. Verified `parse_flag("off ")` now returns False, `parse_flag("ON ")` returns True, and all existing tests pass.
